title: Automated macrophage counting in DLBCL tissue samples using ROF filter
author: Wagner, Hänsel, et al.

steps.title: Select and section tissue samples
steps.instruction: Choose 44 DLBCL biopsy specimens (exclude core‑needle biopsies) from the Lymph Node Registry, use formalin‑fixed paraffin‑embedded (FFPE) tissue, and cut 2 µm thin sections onto slides.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Immerse slides in xylene, then rehydrate through graded alcohols to water.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval in citrate buffer
steps.instruction: Incubate slides for 3 min in pH 6 citrate buffer inside a pressure cooker, then wash in PBS.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare a mixture of CD14 (Clone EPR3653, 1:10) and CD163 (Clone 10D6, 1:100) antibodies in medac antibody‑diluent and incubate slides for 1 h at room temperature; wash in PBS afterwards.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate with donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa 488 and donkey anti‑mouse Alexa 555 (both 1:100) in PBS for 1 h; wash in PBS.

steps.title: Nuclear staining and mounting
steps.instruction: Incubate slides with DAPI (1:5000) for 2 min, wash in PBS, and cover‑slip using mounting medium.

steps.title: Acquire single‑channel and whole‑tissue images
steps.instruction: Capture single‑channel images (CD14 488 nm, CD163 555 nm) as .png files for regions of interest (ROIs) and whole‑tissue scans as .ndpi files; retain all image layers for later analysis.

steps.title: Analyze ROI images with Tissue Studio
steps.instruction: Upload each ROI .png (488 nm and 555 nm) separately, set magnification to 20 × (0.45 µm/px), use Marker Area Detection, set minimal feature size to 30 µm², and manually adjust intensity thresholds per image (CD14 10‑23, CD163 11‑26 on an 8‑bit scale).

steps.title: Analyze whole‑tissue images with Tissue Studio
steps.instruction: Upload .ndpi files, use all layers for background separation, set homogeneity threshold 0.2, brightness 2‑6, tissue minimum size 10‑2000 µm² (sample‑dependent), manually exclude overstained, scratched or folded areas, then analyze CD14 and CD163 channels independently in Marker Area Detection with intensity thresholds (CD14 13‑40, CD163 12‑45 on an 8‑bit scale). Output total area and stained area with annotated image.

steps.title: Analyze images with Halo software
steps.instruction: Set magnification to 0.45 µm/px and use Area Quantification FL v1.2 mode. For ROIs, upload single‑channel .png files; for whole tissue, upload .ndpi files, manually define evaluation subregion and exclude artefacts. Analyze CD14 and CD163 channels independently, setting intensity thresholds per image: ROI CD14 0.1‑0.16, CD163 0.125‑0.19; whole tissue CD14 0.021‑0.097, CD163 0.047‑0.279 (float scale). Output total area, stained area, and annotated image.

steps.title: Train Mask R‑CNN on annotated ROIs
steps.instruction: Randomly select 10 ROIs (20 % of data) for training and 5 ROIs (10 % of data) for validation. Using VGG Image Annotator, place a centered 31 × 31 px square around each manually counted macrophage tag to create training annotations. Convert annotated images to a 32 × 32 × 2048 feature map via ResNet‑101.

steps.title: Apply Mask R‑CNN to remaining ROIs
steps.instruction: Run the Mask R‑CNN implementation on the remaining 35 ROIs (70 % of data) for both 488 nm and 555 nm channels, uploading single‑channel .png files. Discard detected features smaller than 140 px. Export an annotated image with bounding boxes and a binary mask, and record macrophage counts and cumulative area.

steps.title: Perform manual macrophage counting and mask creation
steps.instruction: In each single‑channel ROI image (CD14 488 nm and CD163 555 nm), place a 3 × 3 px cross on every macrophage, then save the crosses into a black‑and‑white mask of identical dimensions as the original image.
